mmvq_rewrite_builds.rule: fewer instructions per dot product wins; anything adding a barrier or lengthening a dependent chain loses; registers beyond ~64/thread lose

eight_vs_sixteen_clients.finding: filling slots moves energy per token more than the cap does; lower the cap after the server is full, not instead

hbm_bandwidth_under_cap.finding: bandwidth does not move with the cap; the L2 at the GFX clock passes 1024 B/clk and still clears HBM peak at 999 MHz; a streaming load draws ~115 W/die at any cap <= 110 W, and the cap binds at ~140 W (1445 MHz) for streaming vs ~90 W for decode

fleet.hyperconverged_rule: all three nodes at the floor first (182 tok/s for 993 W above idle), then caps in lockstep to 125 W (226 tok/s), never higher; HA plan = two nodes inside the envelope, 165 tok/s at 155 W
fleet.production_envelope_note: 125 W is the highest cap inside 1228 W with the host at its RAPL ceiling and every planned addition (4x NVMe on PLX, 2x ConnectX-4 Lx, 2x SATA) at maximum: 30 W margin pinned; above 140 W depends on the host never running all-core while dies are pinned
fleet.governor: not built: read DC total each second, lower the four caps when it passes ~1150 W (the SMC clamps ~20 s after the envelope is crossed)

pass2_gfx906_counters._desc: tools/fa-counters-2.sh (queue 23, 2026-09-08 17:34-18:00): the gfx906 counter set in three passes (GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE SQ_WAVES SQ_INSTS_VALU SQ_ACTIVE_INST_VALU / SQ_INSTS_VMEM_RD SQ_INSTS_LDS SQ_WAIT_INST_LDS SQ_LDS_BANK_CONFLICT / TCC_HIT TCC_MISS SQ_INSTS_SALU SQ_INSTS_SMEM), production build tp4, prefill 4 x 16K (ub 2048); the 'decode' pass (batched-bench 4 x 32K, 16 generated) is dominated by its own 32K prefill, so the one-column decode kernel did not reach the top 12 - the decode-at-depth counters need a -ntg 128 pass (follow-up). VALU busy = SQ_ACTIVE_INST_VALU*4/256 SIMDs/GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE; LDS wait = SQ_WAIT_INST_LDS/GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE (sum over the 4 SEs); per-dispatch counters are sums over the four dies divided by dispatches.
pass2_gfx906_counters.reading: The prefill FA tile kernel: VALU busy 46-47% (the first pass's 45% estimate confirmed), 24 LDS instructions per global load (1.85e8 vs 7.8e6 per dispatch at 32K), LDS wait 7.5-7.6 SE-cycles per GUI cycle (about 1.9 waves per SE waiting on LDS at any time), no bank conflicts, L2 hit 94-95% (the K/V tiles come from L2). It is an LDS-instruction and LDS-latency bound loop at two waves per SIMD - the tile shape at three waves per SIMD is the right first move (S4). Side findings: the MMQ Q8_0 x 128 kernel runs 61% VALU with 6.15e6 LDS bank conflicts per dispatch and 79% L2 hit (S7 material); the GDN kernel 58% VALU with the heaviest LDS waiting (10.7).

governor_threshold_m7._desc: NEXT-STEPS M7 / BENCHMARKS-TODO 7, the DC half (2026-09-08): the 16-client production server (tp4 -np 16, 1300/256 requests) beside an all-core host load (one `yes` per hardware thread, 56 threads) under stepped host RAPL caps; SMC DC total (PZ0G) sampled every 5 s; the job stops itself at 1180 W (200 W die caps throughout; no clamp). dc_vs_host_cap.stopped_at: 200 W (1206 W > the 1180 W guard); 215 W not run

governor_threshold_m7.reading: An all-core host load at the 150 W cap costs the 16-client server 12% (82.3 -> 72.1 tok/s, TTFT +0.2 s): the server's own threads compete with the tenants. DC rises about 1.5 W per watt of host cap with the dies at 200 W caps: 1133 / 1172 / 1206 W at 150 / 175 / 200 W, so 175 W is the last host cap inside the envelope at 200 W die caps (56 W margin) and 200 W already crosses 1200 W. Governor trigger 1150 W with a 50 W host-cap cut (-70 W DC) leaves three 5-s samples before the SMC's ~20 s clamp; at the 125 W production die caps the dies contribute ~300 W less at peak, which is why the host can stay uncapped there.

power_cap_phases._desc: BENCHMARKS-TODO 13 (2026-09-08): the cap curve with the phases separated, production build tp4: decode-only = llama-batched-bench -npl 16 -npp 2048 -ntg 128 (aggregate decode tok/s), prefill-only = llama-bench pp2048 -r 3 (four dies); caps set live with settings/powercap.sh, 200 W repeated at the end. Die W and sclk are the sampler means over the busy samples (prefill has 1-2 samples per cap). Compare power_cap_study (16-client server aggregate, prompt time included): -13.5% at 125 W and -30% at 85 W against -17.3% / -32.4% decode-only and -17.5% / -35.1% prefill-only here.
power_cap_phases.reading: Decode-only at 16 slots and prefill-only fall together (-4.6 / -5.1% at 170 W, -11.8 / -12.3% at 140, -17.3 / -17.5% at 125, -32.4 / -35.1% at 85), both faster than the 16-client server aggregate (-13.5% at 125, -30% at 85), whose prompt reads and queueing dilute the cap. The optimiser's decode factor for 8+ streams and its prefill factor now come from these curves (measured at the five caps); the sclk model below 150 W (-42% at the floor) over-penalised prefill (-35% measured). Both phases run the same die power at each cap; sclk 1689 -> 999 MHz.

Pristine upstream builds at first-parent commits between the fork base 0f3a71be1 (2026-09-02) and master 5d806aa25 (2026-09-08), same recipe (tools/bisect/bisect-build.sh, ccache), same perplexity command (tools/bisect/bisect-ppl.sh). Commit numbers are positions in the 104-commit first-parent list (tools/bisect/commits.txt).
rows: CUDA + ggml: add sparse-fa for DSV4/GLM

Spark2_5ForCausalLM support (parent of the GDN fix)

upstream_ppl_bisect.reading: Two steps, both upstream's, both pinned. Step 1 (+0.27%): e79e4bf66 (2026-08-12), 'ggml-hip : remove -funsafe-math-optimizations' - the HIP build lost -fassociative-math and became IEEE-conformant (upstream's reason: reassociated reductions flipped greedy argmax on RDNA3.5 under MTP); its parent reads 5.5969, it reads 5.6118. The production lineage (fork b10254, stock b10288, 2026-08-05) still builds with the flag. Step 2 (+0.17%): 5fdfa6282 (2026-09-06), the GDN q/k normalisation with eps inside the root (the flash-linear-attention reference form). Neither is a gfx906 kernel; the fork's kernels sit 0.004 under upstream at both steps. Reference perplexity from here on: 5.62 (IEEE build) or 5.60 if the flag is restored (r3, post27). But the branch rebuilt WITH the flag (r3; the flag verified in its compile line) reads 5.6212, the same as without: on today's code the flag no longer moves the numerics - the reassociation-sensitive path was the old l2_norm form of the GDN q/k norm, which upstream replaced on 09-06. Production's 5.5969 = old norm form + fast-math; nothing to restore. Reference perplexity: 5.62.

step1_rows.candidate: e79e4bf66 (position 117, 2026-08-12): 'ggml-hip : remove -funsafe-math-optimizations' - the HIP build lost -fassociative-math (IEEE-conformant FP; upstream did it because reassociated reductions flipped greedy argmax on RDNA3.5 under MTP). The production lineage (fork b10254, stock b10288) still builds with the flag. Pinned by post26 (d86c7d62d vs e79e4bf66); r3 = the branch rebuilt with the flag (post27) tests whether the flag is also behind the branch's 3-4% server-level and 6-12% 8-slot deficits.

tile_table_ablation._desc: BENCHMARKS-TODO 12 (2026-09-08 19:31, second run; the first lacked two builds and used wrong model paths): the fork's three MMQ commits applied cumulatively on upstream b10288 (branch ablation-tile in /root/exabit-llama.cpp-ablation): a = tile-load threads-per-row 8 (39c917808), b = a + the gfx906 MMQ config table with its dispatch guards (f48d37902 + the brace fix), c = b + the partial-k unroll for the Q8_0 vec_dot (b29ea5262). Reference: stock b10288 and the whole fork b10254 (/opt/llama.cpp-mxxm). llama-bench -p 2048 -n 128 -r 3 on one die and tp4 at Q8_0, UD-Q6_K, UD-Q4_K_M; llama-batched-bench tp4 -npl 16,24,32 at 2K (Q8_0).
tile_table_ablation.reading: The gfx906 MMQ config table is the gain: on Q8_0 it alone takes four-die prefill 845 -> 1101 (+30%) and one die 230 -> 315 (+37%), 89% of the whole fork's +34% / +40%; the tile-load commit adds nothing (+0.7%), the k-unroll +1%, the rest of the fork's 81-file diff +2%. It also carries the wide-batch decode gain: 164 / 197 / 217 tok/s at 16 / 24 / 32 slots against stock's 141 / 163 / 181 (+16 / +21 / +20%), level with the whole fork. On the K-quants the table alone is worth 1-2% (Q6_K 660 -> 671, Q4_K_M 747 -> 751) and the fork's +26% / +7% there comes from its K-quant kernel changes. Single-stream decode is untouched by all three (the +3-4% of the whole fork is elsewhere). S1 upstreaming = the config table plus its dispatch guard, with the K-quant kernels as a separate item.

gfx906_branch_8col_check._desc: 2026-09-08 post25b: the branch's (r2) 8-slot decode loss with --no-repack, tp4 llama-batched-bench at 2K, -npl 8,12,16 (and 16,12,8 reversed): the fork's CUDA op fusion on/off (GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_FUSION=1), the custom allreduce off, and production for reference.
gfx906_branch_8col_check.reading: Neither the fork's op fusion (production loses 3% with it off; the branch does not gain) nor the custom allreduce is the 8-column loss, and it is not the first-cell warm-up: in reverse order the 8-slot cell is the last one and still reads 142.7 (production 175), while the first cell (16 slots) drops to 187 from 196-201 - two separate effects. The dense dispatch admits MMVQ to 16 columns identically on both trees, the launch table at 8 columns is identical, and upstream's prefetch is compiled out, so the loss is in the merged kernel body (fork b10912 mmvq.cu + the ported series) at exactly 8 columns; 12 and 16 columns are within 1-3%. Left to the S1b rewrite of the narrow-batch path on the repacked layout, which replaces this path. Production is order-independent to 0.3% (203.5 / 197.5 / 174.6 reversed). With the repack on, reversed: 144.9 / 136.2 / 150.4 at 16 / 12 / 8 - the repacked GEMM's 9-16-row path, 10% below its own earlier readings.

pair_link_sensitivity._desc: 2026-09-08 20:46-20:52 (user's question on the pairs-vs-tp4 fairness): how much the XGMI link matters to a tensor-split pair, production build + gfx906.env, on the ring as cabled (Apple A2326 bridge: two Vega II Duo modules, each die's two XGMI ports = one to the on-card partner, one across the bridge; one link = ~33 GB/s per direction measured, PCIe 3.0 x16 ~13). Pairs: on-card 0b+0e (rocm0/rocm1, one direct link), bridge 0b+1b (rocm0/rocm2, one direct link), diagonal 0b+1e (rocm0/rocm3, NO direct link: two hops or PCIe). llama-bench pp2048/tg128 -r 3; llama-batched-bench -npl 8 at 2K.
pair_link_sensitivity.reading: Taking the direct link away entirely costs a pair 2.5-4.6% of prefill (592 vs 607-620; 583 vs 610-615 at 8 slots) and nothing at decode (38.3 vs 37.8-38.3 single stream, 113.6 vs 113.3-115.5 at 8 slots): the pair's allreduce is latency-bound at decode and only mildly bandwidth-bound at prefill (about 21 MB per layer). A second link per pair (the two-isolated-pairs bridge configuration, Apple A2339, not installed because models above 64 GB need all four dies) could therefore add at most a few percent of prefill and first-token latency to the pairs and nothing to their decode - the pairs' 20% server-level lead over tp4 stands as an overlap effect (one server's prefill beside the other's decode), not a link effect. The bridge pair is 2% faster than the on-card pair on prefill.
